required_claims.text: One rotational treatment builds scalar invariants from radial and angular basis functions and feeds only scalars to the model

required_claims.text: The other rotational treatment carries geometric tensor features of order l >= 1 through the network, constraining every operation to be equivariant

locations.geiger2022: Sec. 4.2; Sec. 4.3; Sec. 4.6; Sec. 6.1 Eq. 6; Sec. 7 Eqs. 15-16; Sec. 8 Eq. 27

required_claims.evidence: geiger2022: all data in the network is typed by how it transforms under the Euclidean group, using irreps of O(3), where l=0 is scalars, l=1 vectors and l=2 the symmetric traceless rank-2 part; Sec. 4.6 defines equivariance and proves that the composition of equivariant functions is equivariant, so constraining each component guarantees whole-network equivariance; spherical harmonics are equivariant with respect to the irrep of matching order (Eq. 6); the tensor product is bilinear and equivariant with selection rules on l and parity (Eq. 16); Eq. 27 states rotation, translation and inversion equivariance together. jacobs2025: recent GNNs such as NequIP, MACE and TeaNet work with highly expressive equivariant tensor representations and operate on them so as to preserve the proper symmetries, and in equivariant networks the additional neighbour attributes are vectors and tensors, giving an atom an environmentally dependent non-spherical character.

required_claims.text: Locality is imposed by a finite interaction cutoff together with decomposition of total energy into per-atom contributions over local environments

locations.jacobs2025: Sec. 4.1; Sec. 4.3 para. 2; Sec. 4.5 para. 1; Sec. 9.1 para. 1; Sec. 4.4 final para.

required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025: the local environment of every atom is represented by an atomic environment featurization; each atom is assigned an energy determined by its type and its local environment; explicit AEFs describe atomic energy through interaction with all neighbours within a cutoff distance; standard MLIPs learn local descriptors for environments encompassing a radius of roughly 5-10 Angstrom, becoming much slower for longer ranges.

required_claims.text: Total energy is constructed as a sum of per-atom contributions, and the training loss must contain a term depending on that sum

locations.jacobs2025: Sec. 3 para. 1; Sec. 4.3 para. 2; Fig. 1; Fig. 2

required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025: an MLIP maps an atomic configuration to a total energy for that set of atoms; each training energy is a total energy for a whole molecule or crystal unit cell because almost no ab initio method allows easy formal decomposition of total energy into per-atom values, so the fitting loss typically must contain a term depending on the sum of energies of all atoms in each configuration; Figs. 1 and 2 show the summation explicitly.

No verified source in this set uses the term 'size extensivity' or states it as a design principle - jacobs2025 describes the summed structure without naming the property. The claim is worded to what is actually supported. Resolve by either (a) rewording the question from 'size extensivity' to 'per-atom energy decomposition', or (b) adding Behler, Chem. required_claims.flag: coverage capped at partial until the terminology gap is resolved

required_claims.text: Symmetry can also be acquired non-architecturally, by training a generic non-equivariant model toward equivariance through a latent-space objective

required_claims.caveat: Single-source claim, verified at abstract and conclusion level only. Related mechanisms in the same family (frame averaging, local-frame architectures) are NOT verified and must not be scored.

required_claims.text: Generalization to system sizes beyond the training distribution remains an open problem with the symmetry constraints already in place
required_claims.evidence: gilmer2017 names designing MPNNs that generalize to larger graphs than those in training as an important future direction, and gives two specific reasons why spatial information makes this harder: the pairwise distance distribution depends heavily on the number of atoms, and the most successful use of spatial information creates a fully connected graph in which the number of incoming messages also depends on the number of nodes; it proposes attention over incoming message vectors as a possible remedy. jacobs2025: the true domain of applicability of U-MLIPs is quite uncertain, with areas of major weakness that cannot easily be predicted in advance - a U-MLIP might give excellent diffusivities for 95% of materials and be quite far off for 5%.
required_claims.caveat: gilmer2017 is a 2017 molecular-property paper, not an MLIP paper, and its models are permutation-invariant and distance-based yet still fail this transfer - which is precisely why it is load-bearing. It does not test per-atom-energy MLIP architectures.
required_claims.distractor_note: An answer asserting that symmetry constraints deliver size transfer is wrong. jacobs2025 Sec. 7.5.3 lists an architecture that cannot capture the essential symmetries and physics as only ONE of two compounding causes of poor transferability; the other is training data that is not evenly distributed in structural or chemical space.

required_claims.text: The locality constraint fails where the physics is non-local, requiring explicit long-range electrostatic or dispersion terms, and its validity is condition-dependent
required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025 describes two strategies. First, implicit renormalization of long-range effects into short-range interactions, which works for homogeneous condensed-phase systems with strong screening; it reports Ceder et al.'s analysis that this success rests on local charge neutrality, which correlates with lower-energy states, while higher-energy states with weaker local charge neutrality have electrostatic interactions that are not well represented by short-range terms - so researchers should be very careful about using only short-range interactions for simulations exploring higher-energy states. Second, explicit long-range terms: Coulomb's law via maximally localized Wannier centres (DeepPot, SCFNN), and DFT-D3 vdW plus electrostatic corrections as explicit energy terms (AIMNet2, MACE-MP0, SO3LR). Fig. 8 decomposes total potential energy into local, dispersion, electrostatic and induction contributions.
required_claims.caveat: This is the boundary condition on Q18.C4 and Q18.C5: the locality ansatz is condition-dependent, not universal. An answer stating locality and per-atom decomposition as mechanisms without stating their failure regime is incomplete.

required_claims.text: Relaxing strict locality through explicit long-range corrections improves transferability to out-of-distribution chemical space, not merely in-distribution accuracy
required_claims.evidence: sanocki2025: the vastness of chemical space makes generalization a central challenge for MLIPs, whose usefulness is often limited by poor transferability to out-of-distribution samples; a systematic evaluation of MLIP architectures with long-range corrections across diverse chemical spaces finds such schemes essential not only for improving in-distribution performance but, more importantly, for enabling significant gains in transferability to unseen regions of chemical space.
required_claims.caveat: Verified at abstract level only; do not score internal quantitative detail. This is the ONLY claim in the set giving directional evidence that a constraint choice measurably improves out-of-distribution transfer, which is the second half of the question. Its direction is notable: the gain comes from RELAXING locality, not from adding a symmetry constraint.

required_claims.text: The locality constraint fails where the physics is non-local, requiring explicit long-range electrostatic or dispersion terms, and its validity is condition-dependent
required_claims.evidence: jacobs2025 describes two strategies. required_claims.text: The strong form — that invariant architectures cannot represent directional information — is false; sufficient message body order recovers most of the gap
required_claims.evidence: Invariant MACE at nu=3 reaches performance similar to an accurate two-body equivariant MPNN using only higher-order invariant messages. MACE L=0 often nearly matches or exceeds competitive equivariant models (3BPA 1200 K: L=0 E 37.1 / F 81.6 vs NequIP L=3 38.5 / 76.2). The paper locates the defect in two-body messages being non-universal approximators, citing Pozdnyakov and Ceriotti, not in invariance as such, and states two independent routes to fix it.
required_claims.distractor_note: An answer asserting that invariant models cannot encode directional or many-body information is wrong. The defensible modality is 'two-body invariant messages are incomplete'.
required_claims.caveat: Sec. 5.1 also asserts that equivariant message passing lifts the degeneracy of most structures, but no source remaining in the set tests degeneracy or symmetrically inequivalent configurations empirically.

required_claims.text: Data efficiency here means sample efficiency only; equivariance carries a compute cost that the founding evidence does not quantify

locations.batatia2022: Sec. 5.2, Computational Cost; Table 2, Time latency row

required_claims.evidence: batatia2022: names the equivariant tensor product as the computational bottleneck of equivariant MPNNs; single-codebase latencies MACE L=0 10.5 ms, L=1 17.5, L=2 24.3 vs NequIP 103.5 and BOTNet 101.2. park2024: message passing extends the receptive field well beyond rc, so communication in spatial decomposition scales with rc times the number of layers; strong-scaling speed-up 13.1-15.4 on 32 GPUs against an ideal 32.
required_claims.caveat: No source in this set gives a controlled compute comparison of equivariant vs invariant at matched accuracy. batzner2022 reports no inference-time or throughput figures at all, so the sample-efficiency result cannot be read as an efficiency result.
required_claims.flag: verify — as of 2026 fused tensor-product kernels (FlashTP, cuEquivariance, OpenEquivariance) have materially changed this cost picture; any cost statement must be dated

required_claims.text: The claim that deep message passing prevents parallelization is architectural, not fundamental: an adapted spatial-decomposition algorithm retains high weak-scaling efficiency at five layers
required_claims.evidence: batatia2022 asserts that decoupling correlation order from iteration count keeps the receptive field small and the model parallelisable. park2024 restricts inter-processor communication to the original rc by exchanging node features and gradients per layer: five-layer models hold 0.95-1.0 weak-scaling efficiency at 2 GPUs and 0.79-0.84 at 32, against 0.83-0.98 and 0.67-0.83 for two-layer models; efficiency rises slightly with more channels and layers because compute grows faster than communication. Strong-scaling saturation traces to GPU underutilization (Fig. S1), not to communication frequency.
required_claims.caveat: Benchmarked on homogeneous alpha-quartz SiO2 where atoms distribute evenly; park2024 notes heterogeneous systems or more GPUs could raise synchronization cost. Relation to batatia2022 is 'qualifies' — both are correct at different levels (architectural vs algorithmic).

required_claims.text: The advantage is regime-dependent: at 10^6-10^7 training structures unconstrained architectures match equivariant ones on accuracy, with the residual cost appearing as training epochs rather than as an accuracy ceiling

Pitfalls for structural optimization and lattice dynamics (non-vanishing net force, non-symmetric Jacobian) are correctable in practice.
required_claims.caveat: Does not overturn C2-C4, which hold in the low-data regime. An answer that presents the 2022 data-efficiency result as unconditional is incomplete as of 2026-02.
